P.10. Summary                                                                                             1655


P.10      Summary
Remark P.10.1 (Completed frontier package). This appendix should be read as a frontier package, not as a
blanket extension of the proved core. What is currently in hand is:
   (i) the finite-stage convergence and geometry of the completed bar tower (Theorem P.2.3, Proposi-
       tion P.2.2);
  (ii) the inverse-limit criteria used by the standard W∞ and Yangian towers in the MC4 package of
       Chapter 34;
 (iii) the compatibility of these completed models with the Beilinson–Drinfeld filtered framework
       (Theorem P.4.2).
What is not yet elevated to monograph-wide theorematic status is the universal claim that finite generation
plus polynomial growth alone suffice for every non-quadratic chiral algebra. The remaining missing steps
are exactly the global obstruction-vanishing argument, the completed 𝐸2 -degeneration argument, and the
finite-stage compatibility needed to pass from the standard towers to a universal inverse-limit theorem.

P.11     Coderived and contraderived categories
The bar-cobar adjunction at higher genus produces curved complexes ( 𝑑 2 ≠ 0), for which the ordinary
derived category is trivial. Positselski’s theory of coderived and contraderived categories [171] provides the
correct replacement. This appendix collects the definitions and key results needed in this monograph; the
chiral specialization appears in §6.11.4.

P.11.1   Abstract definitions
Let A be an abelian category with exact direct sums (for the coderived case) or exact direct products (for
the contraderived case).
Deﬁnition P.11.1 (CDG-algebra and CDG-coalgebra). A curved differential graded (CDG) algebra
( 𝐴, 𝑑, ℎ) consists of a graded algebra 𝐴, a degree-1 map 𝑑 : 𝐴 → 𝐴 satisfying the graded Leibniz rule,
and a degree-2 element ℎ ∈ 𝐴2 (the curvature) such that

                                     𝑑 2 ( 𝑎) = [ ℎ, 𝑎] ,    𝑑 ( ℎ) = 0.

Dually, a CDG-coalgebra ( 𝐶, 𝑑, ℎ) consists of a graded coalgebra 𝐶 , a degree-1 coderivation 𝑑 : 𝐶 → 𝐶 ,
and a degree-2 functional ℎ : 𝐶 → 𝑘 such that 𝑑 2 = ℎ ∗ (−) and ℎ ◦ 𝑑 = 0. A CDG-algebra (resp.
coalgebra) with ℎ = 0 is an ordinary DG-algebra (resp. DG-coalgebra).
Deﬁnition P.11.2 (CDG-comodules and CDG-contramodules). Let ( 𝐶, 𝑑, ℎ) be a CDG-coalgebra. A left
CDG-comodule ( 𝑀 , 𝑑 𝑀 ) over 𝐶 is a graded left 𝐶 -comodule equipped with a degree-1 map 𝑑 𝑀 : 𝑀 →
𝑀 compatible with the coaction and satisfying 𝑑𝑀  2 = ℎ ∗ (−). A left CDG-contramodule ( 𝑃 , 𝑑 ) over 𝐶 is
                                                                                               𝑃
a graded left 𝐶 -contramodule with 𝑑𝑃 : 𝑃 → 𝑃 of degree 1 satisfying the dual curvature relation 𝑑𝑃2 ( 𝑝) =
ℎ · 𝑝 for all 𝑝 ∈ 𝑃 , where ℎ acts via the contraaction.
Deﬁnition P.11.3 (Coacyclic and contraacyclic objects). Let ( 𝐶, 𝑑, ℎ) be a CDG-coalgebra.
  (i) A CDG-comodule 𝑀 is coacyclic if it belongs to the minimal thick subcategory of the homotopy cat-
      egory Hot( 𝐶 -comod) that contains the totalizations of all short exact sequences of CDG-comodules
      and is closed under infinite direct sums.
1656        Appendix P. Nilpotent-completion frontier for non-quadratic Koszul duality


  (ii) A CDG-contramodule 𝑃 is contraacyclic if it belongs to the minimal thick subcategory of
       Hot( 𝐶 -contra) that contains the totalizations of all short exact sequences of CDG-contramodules
       and is closed under infinite direct products.
Deﬁnition P.11.4 (Coderived and contraderived categories). The coderived category and contraderived cate-
gory of a CDG-coalgebra ( 𝐶, 𝑑, ℎ) are the Verdier quotients:

                       𝐷 co ( 𝐶 -comod) := Hot( 𝐶 -comod) Acyclco ( 𝐶 -comod) ,
                                                            

                       𝐷 ctr ( 𝐶 -contra) := Hot( 𝐶 -contra) Acyclctr ( 𝐶 -contra) .
                                                            

These are triangulated categories. When ℎ = 0, every acyclic object is coacyclic (resp. contraacyclic), so there
are natural functors 𝐷 co → 𝐷 and 𝐷 ctr → 𝐷 from the exotic to the ordinary derived category. When
ℎ ≠ 0, the ordinary derived category is trivial, while 𝐷 co and 𝐷 ctr retain nontrivial structure [171, §§3–4].
Theorem P.11.5 (Comodule-contramodule correspondence; [proved]). Let ( 𝐶, 𝑑, ℎ) be a CDG-
coalgebra. There is an equivalence of triangulated categories

                                    𝐷 co ( 𝐶 -comod) ≃ 𝐷 ctr ( 𝐶 -contra) .                                (P.1)

The equivalence is implemented by the functors Φ𝐶 : 𝑀 ↦→ Hom𝐶 ( 𝐶, 𝑀 ) (which sends injective co-
modules to projective contramodules) and Ψ𝐶 : 𝑃 ↦→ 𝐶 □𝐶 𝑃 (the contratensor product).

Reference. Positselski [171, Theorem 5.3]. The chiral specialization is Theorem 6.11.20.

Theorem P.11.6 (Conilpotent reduction; [proved]). If the CDG-coalgebra ( 𝐶, 𝑑, ℎ) is conilpotent
(i.e., the coaugmentation filtration on 𝐶 is exhaustive) and ℎ = 0, then every acyclic CDG-comodule is
coacyclic, so the coderived category coincides with the ordinary derived category:

                                     𝐷 co ( 𝐶 -comod) ≃ 𝐷 ( 𝐶 -comod) .
Reference. Positselski [171, Corollary 4.4]. In this monograph, the genus-0 bar complex 𝐵¯ (0) (A) is a
conilpotent DG-coalgebra, so the coderived category reduces to the ordinary derived category–-this is the
content of Remark 6.11.13.

Remark P.11.7 (Connection to bar-cobar duality). In the setting of this monograph, the bar complex
𝐵¯ ( 𝑔 ) (A) is a chiral CDG-coalgebra with curvature 𝑚0 = 𝜅 (A) · 𝜔 𝑔 (Convention 8.0.2). At genus 0,
                                                       ( 𝑔)

𝑚0(0) = 0 and Theorem P.11.6 applies: the coderived category is the ordinary derived category, and
bar-cobar inversion (Theorem 8.17.4) is a statement in 𝐷 ( 𝐵¯ (0) -comod). At genus 𝑔 ≥ 1 with 𝜅 (A) ≠ 0,
the bar complex is genuinely curved, the ordinary derived category is trivial (Proposition 6.8.7), and
bar-cobar inversion becomes a statement in the coderived category 𝐷 co ( 𝐵¯ ( 𝑔 ) -comod). The Koszul duality
equivalence 𝐷 co (A-CoMod) ≃ 𝐷 ctr (A ! -ContraMod) (Theorem 6.11.22) is the chiral incarnation of the
comodule-contramodule correspondence (P.1).

P.11.2    Relative curved models
The full theory of coderived categories of factorization algebras on Ran( 𝑋 ) is not yet available in the
literature; its development is part of the Stratum II programme (Remark 2.1). Nevertheless, the off-Koszul
statements in this monograph–-where the bar-cobar counit is a curved equivalence rather than a quasi-
isomorphism–-require a precise ambient homotopy category. This subsection defines the minimal relative
homotopy theory needed to make those statements mathematically honest.

Proof. For (a): the bar-cobar counit is a quasi-isomorphism of associated graded complexes by the Koszul

and the eigenspace decomposition is well-defined.

Remark P.11.12 (Relation to the full theory). The provisional coderived category Dco  prov ( 𝑋 ) embeds fully
faithfully into the coderived category of curved factorization coalgebras on Ran( 𝑋 ) by Proposition P.11.22
below: its essential image consists of objects admitting a bounded-below PBW filtration. The full theory
(§P.11.4) additionally handles pro-nilpotent completions, infinitely generated bar complexes, and curved 𝐴∞ -
coalgebras without filtrations. The remaining gap is off-Koszul bar-cobar inversion (Conjecture P.11.26).

P.11.3   Completed ambient for factorization algebras
The full modular programme requires a completed ambient–-the factorization-algebra analogue of the
pro-nilpotent/coderived formalism of Francis–Gaitsgory [26].
Deﬁnition P.11.13 (Completed chiral ambient). Let 𝑋 be a smooth projective curve. Define the following
full subcategories of Fact ( 𝑋 ):
  (i) Algaug,comp ( Fact ( 𝑋 )): the full subcategory of augmented factorization algebras complete for the
                                                                                                          ch
       augmentation-ideal filtration, i.e., those A for which the canonical map A → lim A/Ā ⊗ 𝑛 is an
                                                                                             ←−𝑛
       equivalence.
  (ii) CoAlgcoaug,conil ( Fact ( 𝑋 )): the full subcategory of coaugmented factorization coalgebras that are
       conilpotent, i.e., exhausted by the coradical filtration.
 (iii) Dco ( Fact ( 𝑋 )): the coderived category of curved factorization coalgebras, defined as the localization of
       the homotopy category at coacyclic objects–-those generated by totalizations of short exact sequences
       and closed under filtered colimits (cf. Definition P.11.3).
Pro-nilpotence (condition (i)) is exactly what makes the bar/cobar differentials converge: the chiral bar con-
struction of an object in Algaug,comp lands in CoAlgcoaug,conil . The provisional coderived category Dco
                                                                                                      prov ( 𝑋 )
(Definition P.11.10) embeds into Dco ( Fact ( 𝑋 )) as the full subcategory of objects admitting a bounded-
below PBW filtration. Master conjecture parent: Conjecture 34.9.4 (MC4: completed bar for infinite
generators).
Remark P.11.14 (Status). The E1 -chiral face of this ambient is established: the monograph proves bar-
cobar equivalence in the pro-nilpotent regime (Theorem 8.17.4). The full E∞ -factorization version be-
longs to the Stratum II programme (Remark 2.1). The homotopy form of the modular Koszul definition
(Definition 8.18.7) uses Algaug rather than Algaug,comp because all objects treated in this monograph are
already complete (their bar complexes converge).

P.11.4    Coderived and contraderived categories on the Ran space
                                          ( 𝑔)                                                           ( 𝑔)
At genus 𝑔 ≥ 1, the bar complex 𝐵 (A) is a curved CDG-coalgebra with curvature 𝑚0 ≠ 0
(Example 6.11.2). The factorization structure–-the decomposition 𝐵 (𝑈1 ⊔ 𝑈2 ) ≃ 𝐵 (𝑈1 ) ⊗ 𝐵 (𝑈2 ) on
disjoint opens–-must be compatible with the CDG differential and curvature. This compatibility is not
automatic: it requires the curvature to decompose under tensor products via the standard CDG formula
involving coaugmentation maps.
    This subsection axiomatizes this structure, constructs the coderived category in the factorization setting
by extending the chiral coderived category of §6.11.4, and states the remaining conjecture (off-Koszul
inversion) that separates Stratum I from the full programme.

Proposition P.11.22 (Provisional embedding; [proved]). The inclusion of filtered curved factor-

induces a fully faithful functor

                                       𝜄 : Dco             co
                                            prov ( 𝑋 ) ↩→ 𝐷 ( 𝐶 -CoFact) .

The essential image of 𝜄 consists of those objects admitting a bounded-below filtration F with (gr0F 𝑑 ) 2 = 0.

Proof. Well-deﬁnedness. A provisional weak equivalence (Definition P.11.9(i)) induces a quasi-isomorphism
on associated graded. For bounded-below filtrations, this implies the cone is coacyclic on each stratum Ran𝑛
by Positselski [171, Proposition 3.5] (a bounded-below spectral sequence with acyclic associated graded pro-
duces a coacyclic totalization). By conservativity (Theorem P.11.21), the cone is coacyclic in the factorization
sense. Hence 𝜄 sends provisional weak equivalences to coderived isomorphisms.
   Faithfulness. If 𝜄 ( 𝑀 ) = 0 in 𝐷 co ( 𝐶 -CoFact), then 𝑀 is coacyclic. By conservativity, 𝑀 | 𝑛 is coacyclic
on each stratum. For a bounded-below filtered model, coacyclicity on each stratum implies the associated
graded spectral sequence degenerates to zero [171, Proposition 3.5], so 𝑀 is weakly equivalent to zero in
the provisional sense.
   Essential image. The PBW filtration on bar complexes (Proposition P.11.11(b)) provides the prototypical
bounded-below filtration. Conversely, any bounded-below filtration with (gr0 𝑑 ) 2 = 0 gives a filtered
curved model (Definition P.11.8).

The co-contra correspondence and the remaining conjecture
Theorem P.11.24 (Factorization co-contra correspondence; [proved]). Let ( 𝐶, 𝑑, ℎ) be a conilpotent
curved factorization coalgebra on 𝑋 with finite-dimensional graded pieces on each stratum. Then there is
an equivalence of triangulated categories

                                   𝐷 co ( 𝐶 -CoFact) ≃ 𝐷 ctr ( 𝐶 -ContraFact) .

Proof. The proof assembles the chain-level co-contra correspondence (Theorem 6.11.20) across strata using
the factorization structure.
     Step 1: Stratum-by-stratum equivalence. On each stratum Ran𝑛 ( 𝑋 ), the restriction 𝐶𝑛 = 𝐶 | Ran𝑛 is a
conilpotent CDG-coalgebra with finite-dimensional graded pieces (finite-dimensionality propagates from
the 1-point stratum via the factorization tensor product: near the generic point of Ran𝑛 , 𝐶𝑛 ≃ 𝐶1⊗ 𝑛 , which
is finite-dimensional in each graded piece if 𝐶1 is). Theorem 6.11.20 gives equivalences

                                   𝐷 co ( 𝐶𝑛 -comodch ) ≃ 𝐷 ctr ( 𝐶𝑛 -contrach ) ,                     (P.6)

implemented by the Positselski functors Φ𝐶𝑛 and Ψ𝐶𝑛 .
    Step 2: Factorization compatibility of the Positselski functors. On disjoint opens 𝑈1 ⊔ 𝑈2 , the CDG-
factorization compatibility (P.2) gives 𝐶𝑈1 ⊔𝑈2 ≃ 𝐶𝑈1 ⊗ 𝐶𝑈2 as CDG-coalgebras. The key algebraic identity
is that the Positselski functor Φ𝐶 = Hom𝐶ch ( 𝐶, −) commutes with external tensor products: for a CDG-
comodule 𝑀1 over 𝐶𝑈1 and the tautological comodule 𝐶𝑈2 over itself,

                   Φ𝐶𝑈1 ⊗𝐶𝑈2 ( 𝑀1 ⊗ 𝐶𝑈2 ) ≃ Φ𝐶𝑈1 ( 𝑀1 ) ⊗ Φ𝐶𝑈2 ( 𝐶𝑈2 ) ≃ Φ𝐶𝑈1 ( 𝑀1 ) ,

where the second isomorphism uses Φ𝐶 ( 𝐶 ) ≃ 𝑘 (the endomorphisms of the regular comodule reduce
to the ground field via the coaugmentation). The same holds for Ψ by Lemma 6.11.19(b)–(c). Hence the
stratum-by-stratum equivalences (P.6) are compatible with the factorization isomorphisms.
    Step 3: Assembly. The factorization-compatible functors Φ and Ψ preserve coacyclic and contraacyclic
objects (since they do so on each stratum), hence descend to functors between the Verdier quotients (P.3)–
(P.4). The unit Ψ ◦ Φ → id and counit Φ ◦ Ψ → id restrict to isomorphisms on each stratum (by the
chain-level theorem), hence are global isomorphisms by conservativity (Theorem P.11.21).

Remark P.11.25 (Comparison with Theorem 24.9.27). Theorem P.11.24 gives the co-contra correspondence
for comodules and contramodules over the same coalgebra 𝐶 : a structural property of any conilpo-
                                                                             fact
tent CDG-coalgebra. Theorem 24.9.27 goes further: for 𝐶 = 𝐵 (A) with sectorwise finiteness
(hypothesis (H2)), it identifies the contraderived category of 𝐶 -contramodules with the contraderived
category of A ! -contramodules (the Koszul dual coalgebra). That identification requires the sectorwise
grading because the algebra-coalgebra Koszul duality operates sector by sector.
Conjecture P.11.26 (Off-Koszul bar-cobar inversion on Ran; [conjectured]). Let A be a complete augmented
                            fact
chiral algebra on 𝑋 with 𝐵 𝑋 (A) having finite-dimensional graded pieces. Then the bar-cobar counit

                                              Ω 𝑋 𝐵 𝑋 (A) −→ A

is an isomorphism in 𝐷 co ( 𝐵 -CoFact), without any Koszulness hypothesis on A.
Remark P.11.27 (Evidence for Conjecture P.11.26). Four lines of evidence:
P.11. Coderived and contraderived categories                                                            1663


   (i) Abstract precedent. For CDG-coalgebras over a field, the bar-cobar counit is always a coderived equiv-
       alence (Positselski [171, Theorem 7.2]), without any Koszulness hypothesis.
  (ii) On-Koszul case. Theorem 8.17.4 establishes inversion on the Koszul locus, where 𝐷 co ≃ 𝐷 by Theo-
       rem P.11.6.
 (iii) Spectral comparison. The bar-cobar spectral sequence (Theorem 6.12.6) has matching 𝐸1 pages on
       and off the Koszul locus; the obstruction to convergence lives in higher differentials controlled by
       the curvature.
 (iv) Completed Yangian case. The completed bar-cobar equivalence for Yangian towers (Corollary 24.9.35)
       provides a family of off-Koszul examples where inversion holds in the inverse limit.
The conjecture is the precise formulation of structural gap H1 (Remark 34.9.17).

Notation is organized by category: categories and functors, operads and algebras, configuration spaces and

Remark Q.0.1 (Two-axis 𝐸 -notation; Remark 2.8.7). Bare E𝑛 denotes the little-disks/topological factoriza-
tion axis on real 𝑛-manifolds. The curve-based hierarchy is written only with the suffix ‘‘-chiral’’: E∞ -chiral,
P∞ -chiral, E1 -chiral. A complex curve enters the topological ladder at 𝑛 = 2.

Q.6      Index of key definitions
Index of key definitions with page references.

Canonical anchor labels
Deﬁnition Q.6.1 (A-inﬁnity algebra). We use the curved/filtered 𝐴∞ framework fixed in Definition 6.8.1.
Deﬁnition Q.6.2 (Arnold relations). The Arnold-relation package is the one established in Theorem 5.1.22.
Deﬁnition Q.6.3 (Bar complex (algebraic)). The algebraic bar complex is represented by the DG coalgebra
model of Theorem 6.2.53.
Deﬁnition Q.6.4 (Geometric bar complex). The geometric bar complex is Definition 6.1.13.
Deﬁnition Q.6.5 (Central charge). Central charge is the anomaly/curvature parameter appearing in the
genus-corrected chiral package; see Example J.4.10.
Deﬁnition Q.6.6 (Chiral algebra (BD)). We use Beilinson–Drinfeld chiral algebras as implemented in
Theorem 4.10.4.
Construction Q.6.7 (Chiral bracket). The chiral bracket is encoded by residue/locality operations as in
Theorem 5.1.25.
Deﬁnition Q.6.8 (Topological chiral homology). Topological chiral homology is realized in this manuscript
via the factorization/bar model of Theorem 5.1.34.
Q.6. Index of key definitions                                                                            1671


Deﬁnition Q.6.9 (Chiral pseudo-tensor structure). The pseudo-tensor/factorization tensor structure is fixed
by Definition 4.10.3.
Deﬁnition Q.6.10 (Cobar complex). The cobar complex is defined intrinsically via Verdier duality
(Definition 6.3.6); its explicit distributional model is Definition 6.3.13.
Deﬁnition Q.6.11 (Conﬁguration space). Configuration spaces are as in Definition 5.1.1.
Deﬁnition Q.6.12 (Classical D-module input). The D-module realization used throughout is the one in
Theorem 4.3.4.
Deﬁnition Q.6.13 (E1-chiral algebra). An 𝔼1 -chiral algebra is an associative (but not necessarily commuta-
tive) algebra object in the chiral compound tensor ∞-category of D 𝑋 -modules; see Definition 2.8.3 for the
precise formulation.
Deﬁnition Q.6.14 (E-inﬁnity-chiral algebra). An 𝔼∞ -chiral algebra is a vertex algebra in the classical sense
of Borcherds, i.e., one satisfying locality (skew-symmetry); see Definition 2.8.1.
Deﬁnition Q.6.15 (Factorization algebra). Factorization algebras are fixed by Definition 4.10.3.
Deﬁnition Q.6.16 (Fulton–MacPherson compactiﬁcation). The compactification package is given by Theo-
rem 5.1.2.
Deﬁnition Q.6.17 (Holonomic regime). The holonomic regime for chiral/D-module objects is used through
the Ran-space formalism of Theorem 4.3.4.
Deﬁnition Q.6.18 (Koszul dual algebra). The intrinsic Koszul dual algebra object is Definition 9.3.3.
Deﬁnition Q.6.19 (Koszul dual coalgebra (factorization side)). The factorization-side dual coalgebra model
is Definition 7.7.2.
Deﬁnition Q.6.20 (Koszul operad). The operadic Koszul mechanism used in this manuscript is represented
by Theorem 4.6.2.
Deﬁnition Q.6.21 (Normal ordering). Normal ordering conventions are those in the explicit OPE package
of Definition 19.1.3.
Deﬁnition Q.6.22 (Operator product expansion). The canonical affine OPE template is Equation (20.1).
Deﬁnition Q.6.23 (Operad as monoid). Operadic monoidal composition for configuration operations is
implemented via Theorem 5.1.31.
Deﬁnition Q.6.24 (Pro-nilpotent completion). Pro-nilpotent and completed bar behavior is encoded by
Definition 6.8.14.
Deﬁnition Q.6.25 (Residue map). Residue operations are fixed by Theorem 5.1.25.
Deﬁnition Q.6.26 (State-ﬁeld correspondence). State-field correspondence is used in the CFT/chiral bridge
formalism of Definition 31.7.1.
Deﬁnition Q.6.27 (Twisting morphism). See Definition 4.1.10 for the full treatment. A twisting morphism
𝜏 : 𝐶 → 𝐴 is a degree-shifting map satisfying the MC equation 𝜕 𝜏 + 𝜏 ★ 𝜏 = 0 in the convolution algebra
Hom( 𝐶, 𝐴) (Definition 4.1.9). The set Tw( 𝐶, 𝐴) mediates the bar-cobar adjunction (Proposition 4.1.12).
Deﬁnition Q.6.28 (Verdier duality functor). Verdier duality is fixed by Theorem 6.3.32.
Deﬁnition Q.6.29 (Vertex-algebra locality). Locality is encoded by the factorization-locality principle 4.3.1.
